title: is there a movie that really, really touched you?

commenti.body: Grave of the Fireflies is the movie that wrecked me like no other movie ever has. I’ve only watched it twice, once when I was a child (not a movie for children) and once less than a year ago. I think about it fairy often.

Inside Out. It remains my favorite Pixar movie ever. It deals with depression so well, it makes it easy for children to understand the importance of emotions while also making it relatable to older people who watch. Its one of the only movies that has ever made me cry and will continue to do so

I find myself touched by specific sequences. For example….

My Man Godfrey—when Godfrey (in an almost Wizard of Oz-esque fashion) addresses the Bullock family one by one, showing great compassion and generosity, even to the daughter who >!framed him for the theft of her pearl necklace.!< 

Nostalghia—when the protagonist >!more or less gives his life in order to symbolically “save the world.”!< Which ties in very beautifully to Tarkovsky’s next and final film.

Que la bête meure—little moments of humanity amidst a very ugly revenge story, such as the scene where the protagonist, in the midst of angrily disposing of his deceased son’s toys, finds the boy’s beloved teddy bear and breaks down crying.

Excalibur—when Arthur >!is spared by Uryens, who is so moved by Arthur’s courage that he knights Arthur on the spot and swears his fealty.!<

Leaving Las Vegas—the scene where Ben is fired and given what he terms a too-generous severance check. His boss’s sadness when he explains, “We really liked having you around. But you know how it is….”

Of course there are plenty more, but those are some that stick with me the most.

A lot of Altman's work is so sad and cuts me deep. He depicts the subtleties of a cruel world so well. Big america demolishing mccabe in mccabe and mrs miller, the corrupt world that the decent marlow tilts against in the long goodbye, and don't even get me started on nashville.

I was going through a really rough breakup at the time. I watched Blue is the Warmest Colour and many of the moments, issues and conversations seemed ripped straight from my life. I was watching it with my gf at the time and the intensity radiated off the screen. We managed to laugh about it afterwards though, because there were two couples in front of us clearly expecting a classy movie befitting a Palme d'Or winner, and were not expecting the copious sex scenes.
would you classify its impact as something almost different from that of the other movies? i dont know; when i think about the wind rises, something extremely different and stronger impacts me

Portrait of a Lady on Fire hit me so hard when I first saw it. I’m a guy, and it made me feel for a few hours like I truly knew what it’s like to think and love like a woman. 

Yi Yi, on second watch, was absolutely amazing as well. It felt so much like a complete distillation of life, in all it’s pain, beauty, and mundanity.

but would you classify your feelings towards these films as something different? in the days after watching the wind rises, when i thought about it, something much stronger hit me - a feeling that was different from every other movie ive watched (and even from any feeling i had). im really curious about this, sorry for asking!
